source_text.body:
Plan a week of meals from a fridge photo
A user gave Claude a photo of their fridge and pantry and got a week of dinners, a short shopping list, and meals ordered so perishables are used first.
·
Sep 11, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
The user took a photo of the inside of their fridge plus an open pantry shelf and asked Claude to make a week of dinners using mostly what was already there. Claude produced the meal plan, a short list of only the missing items to buy, and sequenced the meals so the most perishable ingredients got used first, like spinach early and root vegetables later.
How it went
The user says the shopping list dropped to about six items instead of a full cart, and they estimate they waste about $40 less food per week. They also say it solved the nightly no-plan problem; the post does not give the exact prompt or examples of the meals.
Worth knowing
The main catch is that the source only describes the idea at a high level, so if you want to copy it you'll need to invent your own prompt.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Here are photos of my fridge and pantry. Plan [number] dinners for the week for [number] people, with dietary notes: [restrictions or preferences]. Order the meals so the items that spoil soonest get used first, and give me a short shopping list covering only what I'm missing. You're done when I have the meal plan by day and a single shopping list.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/ClaudeAI/comments/1w2oiyn/i_gave_claude_a_photo_of_my_fridge_and_asked_for
